title: Raise the sparse P104 correction floor from 28 to 38 ADDs (no κ)
body:
## Summary

The exact sparse P104 correction from Ali Romman's PR6537 needs at least 38 one-target ADDs, with arbitrary rational coefficients, free nonzero SCALEs and arbitrary restored dirty workspace. This is a scoped written circuit lower bound with exact finite support evidence, produced by Nick Petalas.

```diff
- ADD optimum in [28, 74]
+ ADD optimum in [38, 74]
```

For B output rows each with support at least s>=2, the first output to receive its last ADD requires at least s-1 prefix ADDs. The other B-1 final ADDs come later. Thus every circuit needs B+s-2 ADDs. The source operator has B=28 and minimum support s=12. The generic lemma is sharp as a function of B and s; optimality of either endpoint for this operator remains open.

Credit Ali Romman for PR6537's operator, construction and open circuit gap; PR6529, Rohan Arun / PR6399, Erwan L. / PR6453 and the retained P104 lineage. Classical dependency-graph counting is not claimed as a new method. Original source data and notices are retained byte for byte.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19371027). The task changes from productive helper splitting to a local correction obstruction. No predecessor verifier, native word or whole supplier was replayed as a deliverable.

## Evidence

- Before: PR6537 gives 74 ADDs and the 28 target-write floor. After: PROOF.md proves 38 for the complete same operator, without bounding workspace, coefficient sizes or interleaving.
- The full changed-row support histogram is `{12:3,13:19,25:6}`. Forward rational rows and backward covectors agree for all 799 outputs. Every changed row and support is printed.
- `PASS_P104_CORRECTION_SUPPORT_FLOOR`: all 9,331 three-register binary ADD words through length five, 56 sharp examples and nine rejection controls pass.
- CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict direct normal/optimized checks pass, timed locally at 0.15/0.21 seconds. Both registered VERIFY.json commands pass. These timings only document the CI budget; no speedup is claimed.
- `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at `3dbddeac131dde06cdffaf438fc68d06115b44b2`: all ten files and canonical-base source history pass. Official export integrity and declared-input checks pass. Normal/optimized read-only Git-free replay passes with all eleven exported file contents unchanged.

From the worktree root, the exact local reproduction commands are:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/p104-correction-support-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/p104-correction-support-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-correction-support-floor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-correction-support-floor --check-source-history
```

Any standard-library CPython 3.12 installation can replace that interpreter path. No network access or side-branch history is needed by the direct verifier. ORIGIN.json records the imported source's original head/path/blob/SHA256; its correction array alone defines the exact target. Other imported numbers are neither rechecked nor claimed as new results.

## Limitations

The exact optimum remains in [38,74]. The model fixes the full operator on independent inputs and uses fixed register names with ADD/SCALE operations. Free permutations, multi-target operations, COPY, in-circuit resets, native maps and rounded arithmetic are outside it. A correction specialized only to reachable states of a preceding word is a different question.

This does not improve a recursive invoice, prove a new kappa, supply a physical implementation or change the selected frontier. All five framework assumptions remain. The proof is written mathematics; finite controls do not enumerate all rational circuits or supply formal-kernel acceptance. Independent human review, physical/native/compiler/precision/tape and outer admission remain open. No selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run was performed.

## Open next questions

- Raise 38 using cancellation or the joint dependency structure of the three support-12 rows. Support sizes alone are insufficient, since the generic lemma is sharp.
- Lower 74 with an interleaved literal circuit, prove its arbitrary-input endpoint and charge its complete scalar and physical boundary costs.

## Related open work

- [PR6537](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6537) supplies this exact operator and the credited 74-ADD construction. This result raises its 28 lower endpoint to 38; it does not challenge the upper bound or rerun its search.
- [PR6542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6542) implements the same correction with reversible nearest-grid rounding. Its error and residue questions are outside this exact-circuit lower bound.
- [PR6529](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6529) supplies the scaled native word whose final correction PR6537 replaces. No native or conditional-kappa comparison is made here.
- [PR6538](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6538) checks the scaled native maps, a separate operator obligation; this package only concerns the final scalar correction.
- [PR6551](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6551) changes a caller tree while retaining PR6529's native word. This local ADD floor neither reprices nor audits that caller.

The overlap snapshot covers 521 open PR bodies, 6,526 Discussion records and 8,917 local notes; main, merged formula/object searches and live claims were checked again before commit. Arbitrary diffs, unpublished work and later updates remain limits. No extra computations audited another contribution.

The completion refresh screened all three other account open PRs created since the CLAIM: [PR6572](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6572) changes phase metadata representation, [PR6573](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6573) changes native prefix rounding variance, and [PR6574](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6574) constructs a four-axis Gaussian grid map. None studies this exact scalar correction or computes its ADD optimum. No extra computations audited those results.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/p104-correction-support-floor)`, passed at head `3dbddeac131dde06cdffaf438fc68d06115b44b2` in [run 41616103959](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41616103959). The completed checks were read once; run metadata confirms completed success and the matching head. Local normal/optimized, registered, source-history, committed-byte and read-only export checks also passed. Hosted replay certifies the declared finite checks and source bindings; independent mathematical acceptance remains separate.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated research package. Ten files are added; no shared code, frozen predecessor, selected record or upstream evidence is changed.
